look_here_first: Look for enormous bluish-glaucous, mostly basal leaves and tall, relatively leafless flowering stalks topped by large heads with dramatically elongated dark cones and drooping yellow rays. Compare foliage and cone height, not ray color alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Existing B060 deep review: native in East Texas/east-central Texas, but no confirmed project target-zone counties; planted Austin specimens are not native occurrence evidence.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not count as confirmed target-zone native; scientific FAIL remains independent of learner admission.

morphology_keys.habit: Large, colony-forming perennial with towering flowering stems.
morphology_keys.leaves: Very large blue-green glaucous leaves concentrated at the base.
morphology_keys.heads: Yellow rays droop beneath an unusually tall, dark elongated disk cone.

comparisons.key_distinctions: R. hirta is much smaller and rough-hairy, with smaller leaves and a shorter hemispheric/ovoid dark disk. R. laciniata generally has deeply divided foliage and greenish cone disks; compare leaf division and cone color/shape.

images.role: Tall great coneflower bloom and conspicuous raised disk; basal blue-gray leaf rosette remains later polish.
